narration: Welcome to the Numismatics & Epigraphy gallery, where the very first coins of India are on display. This is the Punch‑Marked Silver Karshapana, accession number NM 20.6/3, a small silver disk just 1.8 centimetres in diameter that hails from the Mauryan era, around the third century BCE, and was found in Magadha, the heartland of ancient Bihar. Unlike later coins that bear a single portrait or inscription, this early piece is stamped with a series of tiny symbols—a sun, a six‑armed motif, and others—suggesting that multiple local authorities or mints may have issued it. The irregular shape and varied punches give us a glimpse into a time when coinage was still a communal, experimental practice rather than a royal proclamation.
